Example Health Opens AI-Assisted Imaging Center

Content is provided for news media use only.

SPRINGFIELD — Example Health today opened a new imaging center that uses artificial intelligence to help radiologists identify urgent scans sooner. The center is part of a three-year plan to expand diagnostic services across the region.

The software flags images that may show strokes or internal bleeding and moves them to the top of the reading queue. Radiologists still review every scan and make every diagnosis, the health system said.

"Patients should not have to wait for answers when minutes matter," said Dr. Morgan Rivera, chief of radiology at Example Health. "These tools help our team focus on the most critical cases first."

The center includes two MRI machines, three CT scanners and a dedicated reading room. It will employ about forty people, including technologists, nurses and administrative staff, and will be open seven days a week.

Example Health said it will publish data on wait times and diagnostic accuracy after the first year of operation, and that the project was funded through its regular capital budget.
